clue.text: Large fellow union member is a dictator

parts.note: large means big
trade unionists address each other as brother

explanation.surface: A burly trade unionist turns out to be a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: BIG BROTHER is the all-seeing ruler of Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's figurehead of total surveillance has become a byword for an authoritarian ruler.

clue.text: Two old shillings, ducks!

explanation.surface: A couple of old coins, darling!
explanation.walkthrough: A BOB was slang for a shilling in Britain's pre-decimal money. 'Ducks' looks like a term of endearment but is the verb meaning dodges.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob is slang for a former British shilling coin, and to bob is to dodge downwards out of the way.

clue.text: Fish for band (queen)

parts.note: a band of musicians is a group
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A fish is wanted for the rock band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(queen)' suggests the rock band Queen, but is the usual crossword abbreviation for the monarch, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: The grouper is a large heavy-bodied sea fish of the sea bass family.

clue.text: Ride wave on cargo ship

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy wave
a coaster is a small cargo ship trading along a coast

explanation.surface: Riding the swell aboard a freighter.
explanation.definitionFit: This fairground attraction is a thrill ride on a looping, plunging track.

clue.text: Noisily tosses in agony

indicators.note: noisily means we go by how the word for tosses is spoken

parts.note: to toss is to throw, so tosses are throws

explanation.surface: Someone thrashing loudly about in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link here, borrowed from the phrase 'in the throes of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Throes are violent spasms of pain or struggle, as in the throes of death.

clue.text: Closing words of Poe constructed with guile

indicators.note: constructed means the letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The final lines of an Edgar Allan Poe tale were crafty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructed' turns POE and GUILE into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the concluding section or speech that ends a book or play.

clue.text: Press knock drink back with humour at first

indicators.note: back means the word for knocking a drink is read the other way round

parts.note: to knock a drink is to down it, to sup

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of humour is taken

explanation.surface: Urging someone to down a drink with a joke to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SUP into PUS; H comes from 'humour' via 'at first'.
explanation.definitionFit: To press something is to push it, applying force against it.

clue.text: Leading Tories are virtuous

parts.note: a team leading is said to be up
Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: The Conservatives in front claim moral superiority.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honourable and of good moral standing.

clue.text: Stanley hit out with some doubt

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Stanley lashes out, though not with much conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges STANLEY and HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting hesitantly means doing it with uncertainty or wavering.

clue.text: Chicken runs protected by heater

indicators.note: protected by means the runs letter sits inside the heater word

parts.note: a boiler is a water heater
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A hen dashes to shelter beside the boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts R inside BOILER.
explanation.definitionFit: A broiler is a young chicken reared for roasting or grilling.

clue.text: Where patients might be directed?

parts.note: split as two words it says hospital patients go into the wards; whole, it means towards the inside

explanation.surface: A question about hospital signage.
explanation.definitionFit: Directed into the hospital rooms, or more generally heading towards the interior.

clue.text: Dodgy bicycle salesman?

parts.note: a shady trader who sells things with two rims and spokes, a playful literal reading of a phrase for a shrewd operator

explanation.surface: A shifty bike merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeler-dealer is a scheming trader who makes sharp deals, and a bicycle is a two-wheeler.

clue.text: Men on board belonging to the crew find some old coins

parts.note: chessmen on the board are pieces
belonging to means of
a rowing crew is an eight

explanation.surface: Sailors find buried treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men on board' suggests sailors, but means chess pieces; EIGHT is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish silver dollars worth eight reales were the pirates' famous treasure coins.

clue.text: European, we hear, got married and finished on board

indicators.note: we hear means the word for a European is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: a Czech is a European from the Czech Republic
to have mated is to have paired up or wed

explanation.surface: A European weds and ends up on a chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means at chess, where checkmate ends the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A checkmated king is trapped with no escape, ending the chess game.

clue.text: Old poet's house given to nation

parts.note: a nation or people is a race

explanation.surface: A classical poet's home is bequeathed to the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Horace was the Roman lyric poet of the Odes.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a celebrated Latin lyric poet of the age of Augustus.

clue.text: What a loaded gun has according to the latest news report

explanation.surface: Breaking news about a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BULLET IN, it describes a loaded gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaded gun has a round inside, and a bulletin is a short official news statement.

clue.text: Posture adopted by coach

explanation.surface: An attitude assumed by a sports trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a sports trainer but is a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means how one holds one's body, and also a horse-drawn passenger vehicle.

clue.text: Ball and chain ruined homo sapiens

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of chain are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: homo sapiens is the human species, man

explanation.surface: A prisoner's ball and chain spells ruin for humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges CHAIN into CHINA. In cricket, this is a left-arm wrist-spinner's delivery turning into a right-hander.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the term names a particular spinning delivery bowled by a left-armer.

clue.text: Give free rein to eluding work

indicators.note: work means the letters of eluding are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Letting oneself off by avoiding work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges ELUDING.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge a desire is to allow it free expression without restraint.

clue.text: Original and very proper — walk inside

parts.note: prim means stiffly correct, very proper

indicators.note: inside means only the inner letters of walk are used

explanation.surface: Something fresh and prim, with a stroll in between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' takes AL from the middle of WALK.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means first in time, primitive or original.

clue.text: Plays around with openers after half a day

indicators.note: after puts the openers word behind the half-day
half a means only the first three of the day name's six letters are kept

parts.note: Monday is a day of the week
keys open locks

explanation.surface: Fooling about with tin openers in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half a' keeps the first three letters of the six-letter weekday; 'after' puts the openers at the end. To monkey is a verb here, to fool about.
explanation.definitionFit: To monkey about is to fool around mischievously.

clue.text: Computer circuit ranking above all others

parts.note: a circuit of a track is a lap
the one ranking first is top

explanation.surface: A machine judged best on the racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer.

clue.text: Airmen rented a resort here!

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means the letters are sorted again

explanation.surface: Pilots hire a holiday spot by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' rearranges AIRMEN RENTED A, and the whole clue describes the sea of holiday resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea between Europe and Africa is lined with popular holiday resorts.

clue.text: Mostly read to the boss

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for read is dropped

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Reading to the manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims STUDY to STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or decorative fastening, also called a stud.

clue.text: Short story and song of magic sandals

indicators.note: short means the word for story loses its last letter

parts.note: a story is a tale
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A brief tale and a song about enchanted footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts TALE to TAL. Talaria are the winged sandals of Hermes (Mercury) in classical myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the messenger god wore winged footwear that let him fly.

clue.text: Most incredible market came back — in cheap shoddy goods!

indicators.note: in means the reversed market word goes inside the shoddy goods word

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbishy merchandise

indicators.note: came back means the word for market is read backwards

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: An astonishing bazaar has returned, full of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' turns the market word round; 'in' puts the result inside the junk word, between its second and third letters. A tall story is an unbelievable one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is one hard to believe, so the superlative means least credible.

clue.text: Owing money for fight

parts.note: money owing is due
L stands for the pound, libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Debts lead to a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal combat between two people.

clue.text: Delayed permit does make a difference

indicators.note: make a difference means the letters are changed into a different order

explanation.surface: A stalled licence application really matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a difference' rearranges PERMIT DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to stall or play for time.
